title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Termly Exam #20 (Term 2)

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #20 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why are liquids useful for drinking? (1 mark)
   A. They can be poured and swallowed
   B. They cannot flow
   C. They are always hot
   D. They keep their own shape

2. Why should each child use their own balloon for the balloon activity? (1 mark)
   A. To make it heavier
   B. To make it burst
   C. To make the balloon bigger
   D. To avoid spreading germs

3. Which of these statements about matter is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Only liquids have mass
   B. Gases have no mass
   C. Only solids have mass
   D. Solids, liquids and gases all have mass

4. How many grams are in 1 kilogram? (1 mark)
   A. 10
   B. 500
   C. 1000
   D. 100

5. Which of these is matter? (1 mark)
   A. Light
   B. Water
   C. Sound
   D. Heat

6. Which of these is a gas? (1 mark)
   A. Water in a cup
   B. A wooden spoon
   C. Flour
   D. The air in a balloon

7. What is matter? (1 mark)
   A. Anything that has mass and takes up space
   B. Anything that shines
   C. Anything that is hot
   D. Anything that makes sound

8. Which of these breaks down and rots easily? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic bag
   B. Vegetable peelings
   C. Glass bottle
   D. Tin can

9. Which of these is e-waste? (1 mark)
   A. A banana peel
   B. An old phone
   C. A leaf
   D. A paper bag

10. Which of these is solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. Dirty bath water
   B. A banana peel
   C. Steam
   D. Smoke

11. Which item is a paper waste that can be recycled? (1 mark)
   A. Banana peel
   B. Old newspapers
   C. Plastic bottle
   D. Glass bottle

12. Which waste goes into a compost pit? (1 mark)
   A. Glass
   B. Vegetable peelings
   C. Tins
   D. Plastic bags

13. What is the job of the gutter in rainwater harvesting? (1 mark)
   A. Stores water
   B. Cleans water
   C. Carries water from the roof to a pipe
   D. Heats water

14. Which of these is a source of dirty water we should not drink? (1 mark)
   A. Water used to wash clothes
   B. Clean tap water
   C. Safe borehole water
   D. Boiled and treated water

15. Which of these can make a river dry up? (1 mark)
   A. Saving water
   B. Planting trees
   C. Cutting trees near it and wasting water
   D. Using rain tanks

16. A school wastes 20 litres a day through leaks. How much in 5 days? (1 mark)
   A. 25 litres
   B. 100 litres
   C. 15 litres
   D. 4 litres

17. What is a good message for a water conservation poster? (1 mark)
   A. Waste is fun
   B. Close the tap after use
   C. Leave the tap open
   D. Water is free for all to waste

18. Which of these is a way of wasting water? (1 mark)
   A. Closing taps
   B. Using a bucket
   C. Leaving a tap running
   D. Fixing leaks

19. What should be done with stored rainwater before drinking? (1 mark)
   A. Drink it directly
   B. Freeze it only
   C. Boil or treat it
   D. Add soil

20. Which of these uses less water to wash a car? (1 mark)
   A. A long shower
   B. A bucket and sponge
   C. A running hose
   D. A large drum poured everywhere

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Write three ways of managing waste in the classroom. (3 marks)

22. Why is used washing water not safe for drinking? Give one good way to use it. (3 marks)

23. Name three gases and say how each is useful. (3 marks)

24. A jug holds 500 ml of water. Musa pours in 250 ml and later takes out 100 ml. How much water is in the jug at the end? (4 marks)

25. A family of five uses a tap that drips 1 litre every hour. Calculate how much water is wasted in one week and suggest what they should do. (5 marks)

26. Convert 3 litres into millilitres. (2 marks)

27. Explain why a kilogram of stones and a kilogram of feathers have the same mass but not the same volume. (4 marks)

28. Write two uses of each of these: solids, liquids and gases. (Choose any four uses in all.) (4 marks)

29. Name two things a farmer can do to save water. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #20 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — They can be poured and swallowed
   Liquids pour easily.

2. D — To avoid spreading germs
   Sharing a balloon that has been in someone's mouth can spread germs.

3. D — Solids, liquids and gases all have mass
   All matter has mass, whatever its state.

4. C — 1000
   1 kg is 1000 g.

5. B — Water
   Water has mass and takes up space. Light, sound and heat are not matter.

6. D — The air in a balloon
   Air is a mixture of gases.

7. A — Anything that has mass and takes up space
   Matter has mass and occupies space.

8. B — Vegetable peelings
   Vegetable peelings are decomposable.

9. B — An old phone
   E-waste means old electrical and electronic items.

10. B — A banana peel
   A banana peel is a solid thrown away.

11. B — Old newspapers
   Paper can be turned into new paper.

12. B — Vegetable peelings
   Only decomposable waste is composted.

13. C — Carries water from the roof to a pipe
   Gutters catch water as it runs off the roof.

14. A — Water used to wash clothes
   Used washing water is dirty and unsafe.

15. C — Cutting trees near it and wasting water
   Cutting trees near sources reduces water.

16. B — 100 litres
   20 x 5 = 100 litres.

17. B — Close the tap after use
   A short, clear message helps people remember.

18. C — Leaving a tap running
   A running tap that is not in use wastes water.

19. C — Boil or treat it
   Boiling or treating kills germs.

20. B — A bucket and sponge
   A bucket limits the water used.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a bin with a lid, put paper in a separate box for reusing, do not litter, make monitors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has dirt and germs. It can be used to water plants or mop floors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirty water, 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for a safe use.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Air or oxygen for breathing, cooking gas for cooking, air in tyres or footballs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each gas with its use.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: 650 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 500 + 250 = 750, 1 mark for 750 - 100, 1 mark for 650, 1 mark for the unit ml.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: 24 x 7 = 168 litres. They should repair the tap or ask an adult or plumber to fix it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 24 hours, 1 mark for 24 x 7, 1 mark for 168, 1 mark for fixing the tap, 1 mark for units.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3000 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 3 x 1000 and 1 mark for the answer.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Both have 1 kg of matter. The feathers take up more space than the stones so their volume is larger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for equal mass, 1 mark for the meaning of mass, 1 mark for feathers taking more space, 1 mark for volume being space.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solids: building, tools, clothes. Liquids: drinking, washing, cooking, fuel. Gases: breathing, cooking gas, inflating tyres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use up to 4.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Use drip irrigation, use mulch, water at cooler times, harvest rainwater.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
